classification.difficultyReason: Read the time for one complete cycle directly from a supplied periodic graph.

content.prompt:
The diagram shows the motion of a swinging pendulum and its graph.

What is the period of this graph?

spec.description: Seven equal-length pendulum positions share one pivot. Left, central and right positions indicate negative, zero and positive displacement; a curved double-headed arrow shows swinging motion. Illustrative angles are unlabelled and do not supply numerical givens.
spec.mathematics: Displacement is negative to the left of equilibrium and positive to the right.

spec.description: Periodic curve starts at zero rising and completes six cycles over 30 seconds. Grid columns represent 1 second; vertical values are unnumbered. Time ticks are labelled every 2 seconds from 2 to 28. Vertical axis has two arrowheads and horizontal axis points right.
spec.mathematics: Curve represented by y=sin(72t degrees), 0<=t<=30. The vertical amplitude is an illustrative coordinate unit; no numerical displacement scale is given.
spec.answerVisibility: All editions; no period annotation is supplied.

answer.worked:
The curve repeats from the upward zero crossing at $t=0$ to the next upward zero crossing at $t=5$ seconds.

$T=5-0=5\text{ seconds}$.
